rationale:
The requirement has one obligation: the review prompt MUST give a report template with four sections.

**Implementation:** the `## Report` section of `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/review-prompt.md` has a fenced template. The template contains these four parts:
- `### Revised text`: "every requirement in the group, as complete directives ready to paste, including new split requirements". This covers the first section.
- `### Edits outside the group`: "revised text of other requirements your changes make stale, or 'None.'". This covers requirements outside the group that the changes affect.
- `### Mechanical changes`: "list new full names and added examples". This covers the third section.
- `### Design questions`: this covers the fourth section.

**Test:** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_gives_a_report_template]` carries a `{test}` reference to the subject. It extracts the `## Report` section with `section` and asserts, using `assert_text_in_order`, that the four headings and the "ready to paste, including new split requirements" and "list new full names and added examples" phrases appear in order. It does not assert the wording of the "Edits outside the group" body, only its heading. The requirement's obligation for that section is to have the section, so I did not count this as a gap.

I found no unspecified behavior or other gaps.

text: The review prompt MUST give a report template with these sections:
- the revised text of every requirement in the group, including new split requirements, as complete directives ready to paste;
- the revised text of requirements outside the group that the changes affect;
- the mechanical changes, including new full names and added examples;
